context.objective: Document how we carry out Carried Interest Waterfall & Clawback, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Three things can start it: a realization event under the fund's governing terms, a required interim clawback test, or final liquidation. The exact interim testing schedule is not confirmed, so I cannot tell you how often the interim tests fall. Once one of those triggers happens, I as the GP Fund Solutions preparer do the first step: I confirm the trigger, identify whether the fund is a whole-fund (European) or deal-by-deal (American) structure, identify which calculation layer I am doing (cash distribution waterfall, taxable income allocation, tax distribution, or a hypothetical, interim or final clawback), record every applicable term and definition from the current limited partnership agreement and amendments, and confirm the version-controlled Excel waterfall model and the as-of date. The output is locked calculation instructions. There are two decisions here. First: is the structure or a governing tier term missing or unclear? If yes, I stop, Legal or the Client gives a current interpretation, the version-controlled model is updated, and the affected model and results are recalculated; if no, I carry on. Second: is the calculation layer or purpose unclear, or have layers been combined? If yes, I stop work on that output, the Client or adviser defines it, and each layer is prepared separately; if no, I go on to step two, collecting and reconciling the cumulative inputs.
What do you compare the cumulative inputs against to determine they are reconciled?

Step two is mine as preparer. I collect the cumulative inputs: cumulative contributions and distributions from the accounting system and general ledger, proceeds and applicable basis, fees, expenses and valuation from the approved transaction, accounting and valuation sources, plus prior carried interest, holdback and clawback from the accounting records and the prior approved model. Then I match opening balances, prior carried interest, holdback and clawback to the general ledger and to the prior approved model. The output is a reconciled input package, and the reviewer reviews that reconciliation. The decision: do the opening or cumulative data reconcile with no unexplained difference? If no, I stop, the calculation is delayed, and the source difference has to be resolved before any calculation, with the reviewer or Accounting deciding; once resolved I come back to the reconciliation. If yes, I move to step three, the fund-specific waterfall. I do not know the exact accounting systems or report names, and the tolerance for a difference that needs action has not been confirmed. Step three, also me: using the locked terms and reconciled inputs I apply only the governing tiers, rates, affected groups and timing in the model, keep each calculation layer separate, and prepare bridge reconciliations for any complex features. Output is a waterfall output for each calculation layer. Decision there: does a complex feature affect the model, like recycling, distributions in kind, permanent unrealized losses, hurdles, blocker entities, notes or loans, or class differences? If yes, I stop until it is supported: I apply only the governing treatment, prepare the reconciliation of valuation, tax, conversion and clawback effects, and the Client and the applicable adviser approve it, which may change model tiers and downstream results; then I continue. If no, I go straight on to step four, the holdback.
How do you determine the holdback amount at step four?

Step four is me as preparer, starting from the approved gross carried interest and the holdback terms. A holdback is carried interest that is temporarily withheld. I calculate gross carried interest, the holdback, and net distributable carried interest, where gross realized carry equals net distributable carry plus holdback. I update the holdback schedule of changes and the effect on member capital, and I document the objective release conditions. Output is the holdback calculation and schedule of changes. I only use the approved percentage, accounting treatment, risk test and objective release criteria, never an example range. One rule first: if the fund is not yet in a cash-carry position, cash carry is not distributed at all. The check I run is that gross carry equals net distribution plus holdback and that every release meets documented, approved criteria. The decision: is a holdback required or is a release being requested? If a release is requested and the approved terms, risk test, schedule of changes and release approval are not all complete, the release stops, the carried interest stays held and it stays open with the wind-down process. If they are complete the release can go ahead. Who owns that holdback decision is not confirmed, and I do not know the actual percentage, the risk test, or who reviews the holdback schedule; those are all open. Either way I then go to step five, the clawback test. That is me plus the designated external tax adviser, at each required test point. I calculate the difference between cumulative carry received and cumulative carry entitlement. Decision: does a gross clawback exist, meaning carry received exceeds entitlement? If no, I record the gross analysis and go to step six. If yes, I obtain the tax adviser's separate tax adjustment and the governing approval, keep the gross and after-tax calculations separate, and keep the assumptions and as-of date; the Tax adviser or the Client decides, and settlement is stopped without that support. Output is the gross and approved after-tax analyses, then on to step six.
After the gross and approved after-tax clawback analyses are prepared, what happens next in the process?

That takes me into step six, the last one: review, approve, post and hand off. It only starts when the package is complete with no blocking exception. In order: first the reviewer independently reviews my work, every changed input, formula, link, assumption and calculation-layer output, and checks all tiers reproduce the approved calculation instructions; the record is the model change log and sign-off. If that review fails, we stop and I correct it, then it is reviewed again. If it passes, the model is locked. Next the approvals: the Client approves the exact version-controlled model version, the as-of date and the final result; the designated tax adviser approves the separate tax adjustment; and Legal or Compliance give an interpretation when one is required. Then the accounting and posting role posts only the approved result under the approved accounting entry and reconciles it. The posting role checks, before and after posting, that amounts posted, distributed, disclosed or sent for member allocation match the exact model version approved by the Client or adviser with no unresolved comment. If that check fails, stop, and reverse or correct under the approved procedure. If required accounts or approvals are missing, posting stops. If it passes, I hand off the approved results and keep the supporting records, and that is the end. One more exception that can come up anywhere: if an outdated regulatory statement or an unsupported calculation or tax treatment appears, we stop using that material and get current validation from Legal, Compliance or Tax; nothing is posted, disclosed or released on stale material. I do not know who has formal internal authority to approve, post or release, or who exactly holds the posting role; that is not established.
What could happen if an incorrect carry result is posted or distributed?

I cannot give you measured consequences, I do not know of a documented dollar impact or a tolerance; the materiality tolerance is not confirmed. What I can say is what the process says to do: if posted, distributed, disclosed or member-allocation amounts do not match the exact approved model version, we stop and reverse or correct under the approved procedure. The reason it matters is that the result feeds other work downstream: the approved net distribution or tax distribution result goes to the teams that execute distributions, the approved vehicle-level carry and holdback result goes to member allocation, the holdback and clawback schedule of changes and release status goes to wind-down until the objective release or settlement is complete, and approved disclosure support goes out only after current Accounting or Legal approval. So a wrong number would flow into distributions, member allocations and disclosure. And on the clawback side, if cumulative carry received ends up above cumulative entitlement, that is a repayment obligation. The known risk points are the fund-specific Excel models: formula errors, broken links, incorrect versions and hidden assumptions, which is why formula changes need version control and independent review. The settlement accounting entries for a clawback are not established, so I do not know how a repayment would actually be booked.
What result is this process intended to deliver for the fund or its stakeholders?

I do not have counts, so I cannot say which is most frequent. The things that stop it, besides unreconciled data and unclear terms, are: the model not being version controlled; tax or legal assumptions that lack support; examples being treated as rules, for instance using an example preferred return rate or example split or example holdback range as a default, where the reviewer stops the process; a complex feature without an approved bridge reconciliation; a holdback release requested without complete approved terms, risk test, schedule of changes and release approval, in which case the carry stays held; a gross clawback without the tax adviser's supported adjustment, where settlement stops; the reviewer's model review failing, which sends it back to me to correct; required accounts or approvals missing at posting; and outdated or legally vacated regulatory material turning up, which goes to Legal, Compliance or Tax for current validation. I should also be honest that a lot is still open: there is no named process owner, model owner, internal approver or posting and release role, no confirmed deadlines, client cutoff, repositories, file naming or retention period, and the fund-specific tiers, rates and holdback and after-tax clawback mechanics have to come from current governing instructions before a fund-specific calculation or release can go ahead. As preparer I must not interpret unresolved governing, tax or legal terms myself; I escalate any conflict between the model and the governing terms, any complex feature, or any result that does not reconcile.
How do you first learn that one of those triggers has occurred?

After a trigger, the GP Fund Solutions preparer confirms it, identifies whether the fund is whole-fund (European) or deal-by-deal (American), identifies the calculation layer, records applicable terms and definitions from the current LPA and amendments, and confirms the version-controlled Excel waterfall model and as-of date. The output is locked calculation instructions.
The preparer collects cumulative contributions and distributions from the accounting system and general ledger; proceeds, applicable basis, fees, expenses and valuation from approved transaction, accounting and valuation sources; and prior carry, holdback and clawback from accounting records and the prior approved model. The preparer matches opening balances and prior carry, holdback and clawback to the general ledger and prior approved model, producing a reconciled input package reviewed by the reviewer.
If opening or cumulative data have an unexplained difference, the preparer stops and delays calculation. The reviewer or Accounting decides on resolving the source difference before calculation, and the preparer returns to reconciliation; if reconciled, the preparer moves to the fund-specific waterfall.
Using locked terms and reconciled inputs, the preparer applies governing tiers, rates, affected groups and timing in the model, keeps calculation layers separate and prepares bridge reconciliations for complex features. The output is a waterfall output for each layer; if no complex feature affects the model, the preparer proceeds to holdback.
When a complex feature affects the model, the preparer stops until it is supported, applies only the governing treatment and prepares a reconciliation of valuation, tax, conversion and clawback effects. The Client and applicable adviser approve it; model tiers and downstream results may change before work continues.
At step four the preparer starts from approved gross carried interest and holdback terms, calculates gross carry, holdback and net distributable carry, updates the holdback schedule of changes and effect on member capital, and documents objective release conditions. The output is the holdback calculation and schedule.
If a release is requested without complete approved terms, risk test, schedule of changes and release approval, release stops, carry stays held and the matter stays open with wind-down. If complete, release can proceed. Either way, the preparer proceeds to the clawback test.
At each required clawback test point, the preparer and designated external tax adviser work on the test. The preparer calculates cumulative carry received less cumulative carry entitlement; if no gross clawback exists, the preparer records the gross analysis and proceeds to step six.
If carry received exceeds entitlement, the preparer obtains the tax adviser's separate tax adjustment and governing approval, keeps gross and after-tax calculations separate, and retains assumptions and the as-of date. The tax adviser or Client decides; settlement stops without that support. The output is gross and approved after-tax analyses before step six.
Step six starts only when the package is complete without a blocking exception. The reviewer independently reviews changed inputs, formulas, links, assumptions and layer outputs and checks tiers against approved instructions; failed review stops work for the preparer's correction and another review. If it passes, the model is locked.
After model lock, the Client approves the exact model version, as-of date and final result; the designated tax adviser approves the separate tax adjustment, and Legal or Compliance provides an interpretation when required. The accounting and posting role then posts and reconciles the approved result under the approved entry.
Approved net or tax distribution results go to distribution-execution teams, vehicle-level carry and holdback results go to member allocation, and the schedule of changes and release status goes to wind-down until objective release or settlement is complete. Disclosure support goes out after current Accounting or Legal approval.
The reviewer stops the process if examples, such as a preferred return rate, split or holdback range, are used as default rules.

steps.handoff: Obtain applicable approvals.
steps.title: Lock reviewed model

steps.actor: Client; designated tax adviser; Legal or Compliance when required
steps.description: The Client approves the exact model version, as-of date and final result. The designated tax adviser approves the separate tax adjustment, and Legal or Compliance interprets terms when required.
steps.handoff: Approved result goes to the accounting and posting role.
steps.input: Locked model and applicable tax or legal support
steps.output: Approved model result and applicable support
steps.title: Obtain result approvals

steps.actor: Accounting and posting role; holder UNKNOWN
steps.completion_criteria: Required accounts and approvals exist and version checks pass.
steps.description: Post only the approved result under the approved accounting entry and reconcile it. Before and after posting, check that amounts posted, distributed, disclosed or sent for member allocation match the exact approved model version with no unresolved comment.
steps.handoff: Passed checks allow handoff; missing accounts or approvals stop posting.
steps.input: Approved result, accounting entry and required accounts
steps.title: Post and reconcile result

steps.description: Stop and reverse or correct a mismatch under the approved procedure. The subsequent route is UNKNOWN.
steps.handoff: UNKNOWN
steps.input: Mismatch with exact approved model version
steps.title: Correct posting mismatch

steps.completion_criteria: Posting checks pass and approved results are handed off.
steps.description: Hand off approved results and retain support. Distribution results go to distribution teams; carry and holdback results go to member allocation; holdback and clawback schedules and release status go to wind-down. Disclosure support goes out only after current Accounting or Legal approval.
steps.handoff: Distribution, member allocation, wind-down and disclosure work continue downstream as applicable.
steps.input: Approved, posted and reconciled result and supporting records
steps.output: Approved downstream results and retained support
steps.title: Hand off approved results

steps.completion_criteria: Current validation obtained; subsequent route UNKNOWN.
steps.data_origin: Regulatory material or calculation and tax assumptions
steps.description: At any point, stop using outdated or legally vacated regulatory material or unsupported calculation or tax treatment and obtain current validation. Nothing is posted, disclosed or released on stale material.
steps.handoff: UNKNOWN
steps.rule_source_ref: Current validation by Legal, Compliance or Tax
steps.title: Validate unsupported material
